question.value: Investigate the variations of the core mass function (CMF) in the W43-MM2&MM3 mini-starburst ridge and establish the link between the CMF shape and local environmental conditions (cloud density structure, evolutionary state, and core mass segregation).

evidence.quote: Among the most central open questions regarding the initial mass function (IMF) of stars is the impact of environment on the shape of the core mass function (CMF) and thus potentially on the IMF.
The present study aims to investigate the CMF variations in W43-MM2&MM3 and establish the link between the CMF shape and local conditions.

findings_qualitative.value: The high-mass end of the subregion CMFs varies across W43-MM2&MM3 from close to or steeper than the Salpeter slope in quiescent/pre-burst subregions (Outskirts, MM51, MM10) to top-heavy in burst and post-burst subregions (MM12, MM2, MM3).

evidence.quote: The high-mass end ($>$1 $\ensuremath{M_{\odot}}$) of the subregion CMFs varies from close to the Salpeter slope (quiescent) to top-heavy (burst and post-burst).
The measured high-mass end of subregion CMFs in their cumulative form varies from being top-heavy, $\alpha\in [-0.95;-0.59]$, to close to the Salpeter slope, $\alpha\in [-1.54;-1.16]$

findings_qualitative.value: Subregions with flat second eta-PDF tails display top-heavy CMFs, whereas subregions with steep second eta-PDF tails have CMFs close to the Salpeter slope.

evidence.quote: We find that subregions with flat second $\eta$-PDF tails display top-heavy CMFs.
We find that subregions with flat second $\eta$-PDF tails display top-heavy CMFs.

findings_qualitative.value: Three out of six subregions (MM2, MM10, and MM3) show evidence of core mass segregation, with MM2 displaying a very high level, but there is no one-to-one correspondence between core mass segregation and a top-heavy CMF.

evidence.quote: In conclusion, our analysis of the core mass segregation suggests that three out of the six W43-MM2&MM3 subregions could be mass-segregated, the MM2, MM3, and MM10 subregions (see 1).

evidence.loc: Correlation trends between the CMF and the basic cloud and core properties
evidence.quote: In that respect, the link between the level of core mass segregation and the slope of the CMF high-mass end may exist but not as a one-to-one correspondence.

claims.hypothesis: The shape of the core mass function (CMF) varies locally with environmental cloud properties within the W43-MM2&MM3 mini-starburst ridge rather than being universally top-heavy or Salpeter-like everywhere.
claims.experiment: Decompose W43-MM2&MM3 into six 0.5-1 pc subregions using MnGSeg wavelet decomposition and fit the cumulative CMF high-mass end of each subregion using a 5000-iteration bootstrap MLE method.
claims.result: The CMF high-mass end power-law index varies continuously from alpha = -1.54 (+0.32/-0.42) in the Outskirts and -1.16 (+0.16/-0.30) in MM10 to top-heavy slopes of -0.95 (+0.15/-0.36) in MM12, -0.93 (+0.11/-0.21) in MM2, and -0.59 (+0.07/-0.12) in MM3.
claims.finding: The CMF is not uniform across the ridge; it varies from Salpeter-like in quiescent/pre-burst environments to top-heavy in dense, active star-forming hubs.

evidence.quote: The high-mass end ($>$1 $\ensuremath{M_{\odot}}$) of the subregion CMFs varies from close to the Salpeter slope (quiescent) to top-heavy (burst and post-burst).
The measured high-mass end of subregion CMFs in their cumulative form varies from being top-heavy, $\alpha\in [-0.95;-0.59]$, to close to the Salpeter slope, $\alpha\in [-1.54;-1.16]$

claims.hypothesis: The high-mass end of the CMF is linked to the high column density probability distribution function (eta-PDF) of the cloud gas surrounding the cores.
claims.experiment: Compute column density maps from the 1.3 mm continuum image and dust temperature map, construct subregion eta-PDFs, fit power-law slopes to the second (s_2, background gas surrounding cores) and third (s_3, cores) tails, and compare s_2 with the CMF slope alpha.
claims.result: Subregions with top-heavy CMFs (MM2, MM3) have flat second eta-PDF tails (s_2 = -0.6 +/- 0.2 and -0.8 +/- 0.2), while subregions with Salpeter-like CMFs (MM10, MM51, Outskirts) have steeper second tails (s_2 = -2.4 +/- 0.2 to > -5).
claims.finding: Subregions with flat second eta-PDF tails display top-heavy CMFs, indicating a correlation trend between the CMF high-mass end and the high-column-density cloud structure surrounding cores, though limited by small sample size (6 subregions).

evidence.quote: We find that subregions with flat second $\eta$-PDF tails display top-heavy CMFs.

evidence.loc: Comparison with observational studies in the literature
evidence.quote: We observed a correlation trend between these power-law indices but the small number of W43-MM2&MM3 subregions and the large uncertainties on $\alpha$ and $s_2$ prevent us from making a reliable estimate of the significance and strength of this correlation.

claims.hypothesis: Core mass segregation directly correlates with a top-heavy CMF.
claims.experiment: Measure core mass segregation in each subregion using both the local core surface density ratio (Sigma_6cores)_massive / mean(Sigma_6cores) and the minimum spanning tree mass segregation ratio Lambda_MSR, and compare with subregion CMF slopes.
claims.result: MM2, MM10, and MM3 are mass-segregated (Lambda_MSR = 5 +/- 2, 2.3 +/- 0.7, and 1.8 +/- 0.4, respectively), whereas MM12 has a top-heavy CMF (alpha = -0.95) with no mass segregation, and MM10 has high mass segregation but a Salpeter-like CMF (alpha = -1.16).
claims.finding: While extreme centrally concentrated hubs like MM2 show both very high mass segregation and a top-heavy CMF, there is no one-to-one correspondence between core mass segregation and the slope of the CMF high-mass end.

evidence.quote: In that respect, the link between the level of core mass segregation and the slope of the CMF high-mass end may exist but not as a one-to-one correspondence.

claims.hypothesis: The CMF evolves from a Salpeter-like slope to a top-heavy slope as cloud subregions evolve from quiescent/pre-burst to burst phases of star formation.
claims.experiment: Classify the six subregions into evolutionary stages (Quiescent, Pre-burst, Main burst, Post-burst) using protostellar core fraction, core surface density, and UCHII region presence, and examine how the CMF slope alpha varies with protostellar fraction and evolutionary stage.
claims.result: Quiescent/pre-burst subregions (Outskirts, MM51, MM10; f_proto = 7% to 25%) have CMF slopes close to Salpeter (alpha = -1.54 to -1.16), while burst and post-burst subregions (MM12, MM2, MM3; f_proto = 41%, 37%, 22%) have top-heavy CMFs (alpha = -0.95, -0.93, -0.59).
claims.finding: The CMF high-mass end correlates with the protostellar fraction (excluding post-burst MM3) and appears to evolve from Salpeter to top-heavy from the quiescent to the burst phase.

evidence.quote: The CMF may evolve from Salpeter to top-heavy throughout the star formation process from the quiescent to the burst phase.

evidence.loc: Impact of this evolutionary stage on cloud and cores
evidence.quote: This is confirmed in 9b, where the slope of the CMF high-mass end tends to correlate with the protostellar fraction, which is the main criterion used to define the evolutionary stage of a subregion (see Sect. 4.3.1).

why_this_data.value: W43-MM2&MM3 harbors a rich cluster with a statistically significant number of cores (205 cores) characterized in Paper III; the 1.3 mm continuum image was chosen over 3 mm for subregion properties because it is less contaminated by free-free emission.

evidence.quote: W43-MM2&MM3 is a useful test case for environmental studies because it harbors a rich cluster that contains a statistically significant number of cores (specifically, 205 cores), which was previously characterized in Paper III.

evidence.loc: Splitting the W43-MM2&MM3 ridge into six subregions
evidence.quote: We chose the 1.3 mm image because, unlike the 3 mm image, it is less contaminated by free-free emission.

why_this_method.value: MnGSeg multi-scale decomposition separates the inhomogeneous ridge into 0.5-1 pc subregions with more homogeneous characteristics; a bootstrap MLE approach accounts for small-number statistics, core mass uncertainties, and completeness uncertainties; two mass segregation indicators (Sigma_6cores and Lambda_MSR) are used in tandem following Parker & Goodwin (2015).

evidence.loc: Splitting the W43-MM2&MM3 ridge into six subregions
evidence.quote: We separated it into subregions of $\sim$0.5–1 pc scales, which, in the framework of dynamical cloud formation, would correspond to cloud subparts with more homogeneous characteristics and star formation activities than the whole cloud.

Given the small-number statistics for the core sample of each W43-MM2&MM3 subregion, we did not directly apply the (cite: alstott2014) method to their CMF but used it in a bootstrap procedure that simultaneously estimates the most likely CMF power-law index and its uncertainty.
We followed the recommendations of (cite: parkerGoodwin2015) and used two different indicators in tandem.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Direct application of the Alstott et al. (2014) MLE method and linear regression on the cumulative CMF without bootstrapping (used as a validation check on the total ridge CMF).

evidence.quote: To test the validity of our approach, we compared the power-law index fitted by the bootstrapping procedure described above with those directly fitted by the method of (cite: alstott2014) and a linear regression on its cumulative form.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Assuming a constant dust temperature across all cores or all pixels when computing core masses and column density eta-PDFs (tested and found to change CMF indices by at most 18% and eta-PDF tail slopes by <= 10%).

evidence.quote: taking a constant dust temperature for all cores, including the most massive ones associated with hot cores, would change the power-law indices fitted to the subregion CMF by at most $18\%$.

The assumption on the dust temperature used to compute the column density image has a negligible effect on the $\eta$-PDFs since, with a constant temperature on all pixels, the power-law exponents of their $s_2$ and $s_3$ tails are not changed by more than $10\%$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Applying the Paper III optical thickness correction to the column density map (would only change values by 15% toward the center of four cores).

referee_caveats_inferred: Subregion boundaries were defined visually along inflection points of the wavelet-filtered map rather than via an automated segmentation algorithm, introducing subjective boundary choices.

Adding a constant per-subregion column density offset from 25'' Herschel data to 0.46'' ALMA 12 m continuum images is only a first-order approximation for missing short-spacing (7 m and Total Power) flux.
Correlation claims between CMF slope, eta-PDF slope, and protostellar fraction rely on only 6 subregions (4 with measured s_2) with overlapping bootstrap uncertainty intervals.
